questions.q: The domain of the function $f(x)=\sqrt{x-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$ is
questions.solution:
For $f(x)$ to be defined, we must have $x-\sqrt{1-x^{2}} \geq 0$ or $\quad x \geq \sqrt{1-x^{2}} \gt 0\therefore \quad x^{2} \geq 1-x^{2}$ or $x^{2} \geq \frac{1}{2}$

Also, $1-x^{2} \geq 0$ or $x^{2} \leq 1$.

Now, $x^{2} \geq \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow\left(x-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\left(x+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \geq 0\Rightarrow x \leq-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ or $x \geq \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Also, $x^{2} \leq 1 \Rightarrow(x-1)(x+1) \leq 0\Rightarrow-1 \leq x \leq 1$

Thus, $x \gt 0, x^{2} \geq \frac{1}{2}$ and $x^{2} \leq 1\Rightarrow x \in\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, 1\right]$

questions.q: The probability that certain electronic component fails when first used is 0.10 . If it does not fail immediately, the probability that it lasts for one year is $0.99 .$ The probability that a new component will last for one year is
questions.solution:
Probability that the electronic component fails when first used is $P(F)=0.10$. Therefore, $P\left(F^{\prime}\right)=1-P(F)=0.90$

$\text { Then, } P(E)=P(F) P\left(\frac{E}{F}\right)+P\left(F^{\prime}\right) P\left(\frac{E}{F^{\prime}}\right)$

[total probability theorem] $=0.10 \times 0+0.90 \times 0.99=0.891$

questions.q: The upper half of an inclined plane with inclination $\phi$ is perfectlysmooth while the lower halfis rough. A body starting from rest at the top will again come to rest at the bottom if the coefficient of friction for the lower half is given by
questions.solution:
Acceleration of block while sliding down upper half $=\mathrm{g} \sin \phi$

retardation of block while sliding down lower half $=-(\mathrm{g} \sin \phi-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \phi)$

For the block to come to rest at the bottom, acceleration in I half = retardation in II half.

$\mathrm{g} \sin \phi=-(\mathrm{g} \sin \phi-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \phi)\Rightarrow \mu=2 \tan \phi$

Alternative method: According to work-energy theorem, $\mathrm{W}=\Delta \mathrm{K}=0$

(Since initial and final speeds are zero)

$\therefore$ Work done by friction $+$ Work done by gravity $=0$ i.e., $-(\mu \mathrm{mg} \cos \phi) \frac{\ell}{2}+\mathrm{mg} \ell \sin \phi=0$

or $\frac{\mu}{2} \cos \phi=\sin \phi$ or $\mu=2 \tan \phi$
